note: The game's copy of the prologue's rules (Alpha 0.3 §2; docs/prologue-content/: sites_prologue.json, life.json, custody.json, preorders.json and events_prologue.json's decision quarters and offers), reshaped into structured fields. Values are the pack's; 'designed' marks the scope's designed values (§2.8, §6). Where the pack's text had to become numbers, the reading is in the field's note.

drain_per_quarter.note: at each quarter end while the load at a household site is above its threshold (scope §2.3)

household.patience_note: Prologue choice: after a forced cut quarter the household calms down to half its start patience.

bandwidth_costs.note: Prologue choice, as Act I: building a site (the home rig, moving out, the small unit) and selling from the Plan screen cost 1 Bandwidth each (balance.ts bandwidth.build / sellTreasury). Buying machines, moving coins, conferences and vanity cost none.

move_out.rent_note: Years before the first listed use the first listed value; others the latest listed at or before (the pack's national averages; a college town would be 10–20% lower: a tuning lever, scope P4).

move_back.note: Owner (P5.0, P6): moving back home costs 1 Bandwidth; rent stops, household power returns, patience resets to 50, the income doesn't return; the sites go back to the bedroom + home rig and machines that don't fit are sold at the used price. At quarter end, still short of cash after selling coins, a moved-out player moves back home before machines are sold or the game ends.

wallet_loss.pc_class_note: Owner (P5.0): a backup lasts until you buy a new PC or move out (scope §2.7), not on buying a GPU. The PC isn't for sale in the prologue, so today only moving out lapses it.

sell_caps_usd_week.note: Designed weekly caps on coin sales (scope §2.8, P0-16: the pack has no volume series). Realised price = market × (1 − impact × sale ÷ cap). Unfilled orders carry to the next week. Forum offers are outside the cap. 2009 has no market (price $0).

ships_quarter.note: P4 tuning (designed value): an on-time unit, whenever it was ordered, arrives in 2013Q3 and mines from 2013Q4 (the pack's balance anchor: on time = 7 Oct 2013, ≈3.3× its cost sold weekly). Late and very late count their quarters from it. Before: on time = promised_quarters after the order, which gave 7.9× (2013Q1 order) to 34× (2012Q4 order) on time and a 3.1–16× average, against the scope's 1.2–1.8×.

preorders.note: Delay rolled at order time on its own seeded stream. Delay quarters count after the promised delivery (on time = delivered after promised_quarters). The conference contact moves 10 points into on-time, taken from severe first, then never.

offer_note: An offer opens in its quarter (from its date) and stays in the tray until the end of the next decision quarter at or after it (a Prologue choice: most offer quarters auto-play).

spare_pc.note: Doc 51 v1.6 §17 (designed): the starter PC can be bought again as a Spare PC (new only, $350 in machines_prologue.json) into the home rig; 4 CPU PCs in all, the starter included.

altcoin_selling_limits.note: Doc 51 v1.0 §5, doc 53 A6: a sale is free up to free_share of the year's average daily volume (USD); each further step_share of it moves the price down by slippage_per_step; hard_cap_share is the most one week may sell. Altcoins sit in your own wallet (an exchange collapse moves price only).
altcoin_selling_limits.volume_rule: use the week's real daily volume (market file, CoinMarketCap [A]) where present, else the year's average below

altcoin_handover.note: Doc 51 v1.0 §5: altcoins are sold over 2016Q4 within the selling limits at the weekly prices; whatever is left converts at the 2016Q4 close x this; no altcoin enters Act I.

career_markers_note: The chapter report's career graph (wireframe P0-07): labelled quarters, display only.
